Calculation Grid Rules

Place the numbers 1 to 9 so that every calculation works out.

The rules

The grid
Nine squares in three rows and three columns, with an operator between neighbouring squares (+, −, ×, ÷) and the result at the end of every row and below every column. Every number from 1 to 9 goes into exactly one square. Some numbers are given.
Left to right
A row is worked out from left to right, a column from top to bottom - one step after the other, without "multiplication before addition": 3 + 4 × 2 gives 7 × 2 = 14, not 11. Some school versions of this puzzle use the usual order of operations; here it is always left to right.
Whole numbers
Every intermediate result and every result is a whole number greater than 0, so a division always comes out even.
Levels
Easy: only + and −, 4 numbers given. Medium: also ×, 3 given. Hard: all four operators with at least one ÷, 2 given. Every puzzle has exactly one solution and can be solved without guessing.
Playing
Tap an empty square, then a number below the board; tap the number again or Clear to empty the square. A number already used in another square moves here. Once a row or column is full, a tick or a cross shows whether it works out. The Hint button marks a wrong number first, otherwise it fills in a square that can be worked out now.

Example

A solved Calculation Grid. Middle row: 9 − 1 = 8, then 8 × 3 = 24 - worked from left to right, not 9 − 3 = 6.
